title: NOFIS: Normalizing Flow for Rare Circuit Failure Analysis
problem: Conventional Monte Carlo methods for estimating rare IC failure probability are inefficient, requiring exorbitant sample sizes. Accurate rare failure probability estimation is essential yet challenging for ensuring circuit reliability.
motivation: Accurate rare failure probability estimation is crucial for ensuring the proper and reliable functioning of integrated circuits.
method: Estimating rare circuit failures is impractical through direct simulation because failures are so infrequent you'd need billions of runs to observe even one. NOFIS addresses this by using normalizing flows (machine learning models that learn to transform simple random distributions into complex ones) to automatically learn a proposal distribution—a specialized probability distribution designed to concentrate sampling in the rare failure regions. It learns this distribution by minimizing KL divergence (a measure of how different two probability distributions are), then uses importance sampling (a technique that weights rare samples more heavily) to accurately estimate the overall failure probability.
key_novelty: The innovation is using normalizing flows to learn proposal distributions for importance sampling in rare circuit failure probability estimation.
contributions: NOFIS method combining normalizing flows with importance sampling for rare event probability estimation
Learning sequence of proposal distributions via KL divergence minimization for nested subset events
Superior accuracy over baseline Monte Carlo approaches demonstrated across 10 quantitative experiments
